cluster_name: France and Spain wildfires force 200,000 evacuations near Bordeaux and Madrid
tldr: Headlines across 24 outlets in 15 countries lead almost universally with mass-displacement statistics — evacuation figures ranging from 80,000 to 220,000 — making quantified human scale the dominant advertised signal across all geographic and editorial perspectives. The headline layer contains no climate attribution whatsoever; the only departure from the evacuation-count template is Le Parisien, whose two French-language titles avoid statistics entirely and address firefighter exhaustion and wildfire-induced mental health trauma — a framing completely invisible in every non-French outlet's headlines.
event_summary: Wildfires swept southwestern France and central Spain on July 24-25, 2026, forcing more than 200,000 people to flee near Bordeaux and Madrid; Spain declared a national emergency and France activated the EU Civil Protection Mechanism.

frames.sub_frame: Mental health toll; survivors sheltering indoors

single_outlet_findings.finding: Both Le Parisien headlines are the only titles in the corpus to avoid evacuation statistics entirely — one addresses firefighter exhaustion and fear of further deaths, the other addresses mental health trauma — a humanitarian framing completely invisible in all non-French headlines.

Only outlet to open with a survivor testimony ('You couldn't breathe') rather than an evacuation number, centering embodied experience over quantitative scale in a way unique among Southeast Asian establishment press.

Only outlet to single out British nationals as a specific affected demographic — 'Brits among 200,000 fleeing scorched tourist areas' — anchoring the pan-European crisis to UK audience identity rather than a neutral count.
Only outlet to foreground EU collective action ('EU deploys aircraft') in the headline itself rather than centering human displacement, emphasising institutional response over humanitarian scale.

Reports only '80,000 flee' — roughly one-third of the 220,000 figure cited by BBC World — the lowest evacuation figure across all outlets, suggesting early snapshot timing rather than deliberate minimisation.

bottom_line: The headline layer of this wildfire story is a near-uniform row of evacuation statistics: 24 outlets in 15 countries used their titles to broadcast a displacement number, with no outlet naming climate change as a driver anywhere in a headline despite three outlets carrying that framing in body text. The sole variation came from French domestic press, where Le Parisien's two headlines broke the template entirely to address firefighter exhaustion and wildfire-induced mental health damage.
